events.title: The Past Didn't Go Anywhere: Fundamentals > AI
events.description:
For decades, our industry has predicted that the next wave of technology would replace software developers. From COBOL to the dot-com boom, DevOps, and now AI, each shift has promised to fundamentally change our profession.
Yet developers are still here.

The difference is that every wave has demanded new skills, not fewer developers. As AI continues to reshape software engineering, one thing has become increasingly clear: the developers who thrive will be the ones who understand the fundamentals.

Join CIJUG as Dustin Thostenson explores why design patterns, system thinking, effective communication, testing, and quality engineering remain just as important today as they've ever been. Rather than focusing on AI tools themselves, this session examines how developers can avoid common pitfalls like AI-generated technical debt, missed business outcomes, and systems that become increasingly difficult to understand and maintain.
You'll learn practical approaches to defining problems clearly, designing systems with well-defined responsibilities, and writing tests that build confidence instead of simply checking boxes.

**About the Speaker**
Dustin Thostenson is an independent consultant leading Delta3Consulting. Over the course of his career, he has served as a developer, mentor, trainer, and agile coach, with a passion for helping people grow and teams deliver better outcomes. Dustin also helps lead the Iowa .NET User Group and is an active volunteer in the Central Iowa technology community.

events.title: CIJUG Social Networking Event
events.description:
Join the Central Iowa Java User Group on Wednesday, September 16th from 5:30 – 7pm at Source Allies for food, drinks, and conversation at a CIJUG social! No presentations. No coding sessions. Just a chance to spend some time with our local CIJUG members.

Our regular meetups give us opportunities to learn about Java, the JVM, software engineering, and new technologies. This month, we're setting the technical topics aside and making time to get to know the people who make up our community.
Come meet other developers from around Iowa, catch up with people you've met at past CIJUG events, make some new connections, and talk about whatever is on your mind. Java is optional.

It doesn’t matter if you've been attending CIJUG for years or have never been to one of our events before, you’re welcome to stop by.

Wednesday, September 16th, 2026
5:30 to 7:00 PM
Hosted at Source Allies
Food and drinks will be provided – hope to see you there!

events.title: CIJUG Lightning Talks
events.description:
CIJUG returns on Thursday, October 22nd from 5:30 to 7pm for a Lightning Talks night at Source Allies!

Lightning talks are a chance to hear several quick presentations in one evening. This month’s lineup covers everything from JVM internals to local AI to using your skills for good.

**Garbage Out**
Ben DeMouth, Source Allies
A look at how different JVM garbage collection configurations work and the tradeoffs each one makes.

**Local AI Image Generation Is Getting Disturbingly Good**
Nathan Halko
Local AI image and video models have come a long way in the last year. Nathan will show what you can now run on a typical gaming PC and how people are using it to make money online.

**Did Any of It Matter? Why Shipping Software Isn’t the Same as Delivering Value**
Adam Horning
A short, non-technical talk from a Product Owner perspective on the difference between shipping features and actually making a difference for the customer or business.

**Turning Tech Skills Into Community Impact**
Dellen Burk-Flores, President of dsmHack

How dsmHack’s 48-hour charity hackathons bring tech professionals together to build solutions for local nonprofits, and how you can get involved.

After the talks, stick around for questions and conversation with the speakers and other members of the community.

Hosted in person at Source Allies. Food and drinks provided. Please RSVP so we can get a head count!
